A negative gate voltage is applied to a MOS capacitor on p-type silicon. What gathers at the surface?
questions.explain: A negative gate attracts majority holes into accumulation.

questions.stem: A modest positive gate voltage is applied to a MOS capacitor on p-type silicon. What happens before inversion?
choices: Holes move away from the surface
Electrons leave the surface and holes accumulate
questions.explain: The positive gate repels holes and exposes ionized acceptors.

questions.stem: What forms at the surface of a p-type MOS capacitor in strong inversion?
choices: A higher density of mobile holes
questions.explain: Electrons become the dominant mobile carriers at the surface.

questions.stem: The oxide thickness is doubled at fixed permittivity and area. What happens to C_ox per area?
questions.explain: Oxide capacitance per area equals ε_ox/t_ox.

questions.stem: An enhancement NMOS has V_GS = 0 and a positive threshold voltage. What is its ideal state?
questions.explain: An enhancement NMOS needs gate voltage above threshold to form a channel.

questions.stem: An enhancement NMOS has V_GS = 2.5 V, V_T = 0.5 V, and V_DS = 1 V. In which ideal long-channel region does it operate?
questions.explain: V_OV = 2.0 V. The transistor is on and V_DS is smaller than V_OV.

questions.stem: At fixed gate voltage above threshold, an NMOS reaches V_DS = V_OV. What happens at the drain end?
questions.explain: The inversion charge at the drain end approaches zero at the onset of saturation.

questions.stem: A long-channel NMOS in saturation doubles its overdrive while k stays fixed. What happens to I_D?
questions.explain: Ideal saturation current scales with V_OV^2.

questions.stem: Two otherwise identical long-channel MOSFETs run in saturation at the same overdrive. One has twice the width. How does its drain current compare?
choices: It is four times as large
questions.explain: At fixed length, oxide and mobility, k and I_D both scale with width.

questions.stem: If a MOSFET has larger g_m at its operating point, what does the same small ΔV_GS produce?
choices: A larger change in drain current
A smaller change in drain current
The same change in drain current
questions.explain: Transconductance is the local ratio of drain-current change to gate-voltage change.

questions.stem: In an NPN BJT in forward-active operation, which bias combination applies?
questions.explain: Forward bias injects carriers from the emitter, and the reverse-biased collector junction collects them.

questions.stem: Why does a thin base generally help BJT current gain?
choices: Less injected charge recombines in the base
More charge is trapped permanently in the base
Collector voltage stops affecting the device
questions.explain: More injected carriers reach the collector before recombining.

questions.stem: At fixed I_B, what usually happens to I_C if V_CE increases in the forward-active region?
questions.explain: Collector depletion extends into the base, reducing the neutral base width.

questions.stem: Two BJTs have the same collector current. Which has the larger output resistance?
choices: They are equal regardless of V_A
The current does not allow comparison
questions.explain: The Early-effect approximation is r_o ≈ V_A/I_C.

questions.stem: An NPN switch has both junctions forward biased. What is the operating state?
questions.explain: In BJT saturation both junctions are forward biased.

questions.stem: A CMOS inverter receives a low input. Which path pulls the output high?
questions.explain: PMOS is on and NMOS is off for a valid low input.

questions.stem: A CMOS inverter receives a high input. What happens to its output?
questions.explain: NMOS is on and PMOS is off for a valid high input.

questions.stem: Why does an ideal CMOS inverter draw little static supply current at a steady logic level?
choices: One device is off in each steady state
The load is always shorted to ground
The output voltage is always zero
questions.explain: There is no steady conducting path from supply to ground in the ideal model.

questions.stem: A CMOS inverter switches at the same rate and voltage after its load capacitance doubles. What happens to dynamic power?
questions.explain: At fixed supply, activity and frequency, dynamic power is proportional to load capacitance.

questions.stem: At fixed switching activity, frequency and load, what happens to ideal CMOS dynamic power when V_DD is halved?
questions.explain: The switching-power model is P_dyn = a C_L V_DD^2 f.

pages.title: MOS capacitor states
body: On p-type silicon, negative gate bias causes hole accumulation. Modest positive bias depletes holes. Strong positive bias causes electron inversion.

pages.title: Oxide capacitance and threshold
body: C_ox = ε_ox/t_ox per unit area. Thinner oxide increases capacitance.
Strong inversion is near ψ_s ≈ 2 φ_F. Here V_T in MOSFET equations is the gate threshold. The thermal voltage in φ_F is kT/q.

pages.title: MOSFET operating regions
body: Enhancement NMOS is normally off. A depletion-mode device has a channel at zero gate bias. NMOS passes a strong logic 0.
For V_OV = V_GS − V_T > 0, V_DS below V_OV gives the linear region. Pinch-off begins at V_DS = V_OV. Reverse body bias raises V_T.

pages.title: MOSFET current, gain and speed
body: For long-channel saturation, I_D,sat ≈ (k/2)V_OV^2, where k = μ C_ox W/L.
Use g_m ≈ 2 I_D/V_OV and f_T ≈ g_m/(2πC_G) in the simplified model. Conduction loss is I_D^2 R_DS(on).

pages.title: BJT junctions and current gain
body: In forward-active operation, emitter–base is forward biased and collector–base is reverse biased. With both forward biased, the BJT is in saturation.
α = I_C/I_E and β = I_C/I_B = α/(1 − α). A thinner base reduces recombination and cuts diffusion transit time, which scales with base width squared.

pages.title: The Early effect
body: Increasing V_CE expands collector depletion into the base, reducing its effective width and raising I_C slightly at fixed base drive.
Use r_o ≈ V_A/I_C. Larger V_A gives flatter output curves.

pages.title: BJT load line
body: For the simple resistive collector circuit, V_CE = V_CC − I_C R_L. The current-axis intercept is V_CC/R_L.
The maximum transistor power along the ideal DC load line is V_CC^2/(4R_L).

pages.title: CMOS inverter
body: Low input turns PMOS on and pulls the output high. High input turns NMOS on and pulls the output low.
Ideal static power is low. Switching power is P_dyn = a C_L V_DD^2 f, where a is switching activity.
